title_prefix: A boolean wire field is true only for th
mechanism: Core's bool unserializer assigns the raw byte to a bool -- `uint8_t f = ser_readdata8(s); a = f;` (refs/bitcoin/src/serialize.h:277 at d3056bc) -- so every nonzero byte is true. Three places on our side test equality with 1 instead: the generated :bool codec row (src/serialization/message-macro.lisp:109, `(= (br-read-u8 br) 1)`), the version message's hand-written relay :read form which repeats the same test (src/serialization/messages.lisp:206-210), and parse-sendcmpct-payload (src/serialization/messages.lisp:604-610, `(values (= announce 1) version)`). Any byte other than 0 or 1 therefore reads as FALSE where Core reads TRUE. Core's consumers take the value straight: `vRecv >> fRelay` then `tx_relay->m_relay_txs = fRelay` / `if (fRelay) pfrom.m_relays_txs = true` (net_processing.cpp:3647, 3693-3695), and `vRecv >> sendcmpct_hb` then `nodestate->m_requested_hb_cmpctblocks = sendcmpct_hb` / `pfrom.m_bip152_highbandwidth_from = sendcmpct_hb` (:3910, :3918-3921).
consequence: A peer whose VERSION carries fRelay = 2 is recorded as not wanting transactions: peer-tx-relay-p returns NIL, so it is excluded from tx inv announcements and its tx getdata is ignored for the life of the connection (src/networking/peer.lisp:777-789, consumed at src/networking/protocol.lisp:2142, :2896, :3086, :3150 and reported as relaytxes=false by getpeerinfo, src/rpc/net.lisp:210), where Core would relay to it. A sendcmpct with announce = 2 does not put us in the peer's high-bandwidth set. One sharper edge the finding did not name: with -txreconciliation on, a peer that sends sendtxrcncl after a VERSION with fRelay = 2 is treated as a protocol violation and DISCONNECTED (src/networking/peer.lisp:880-887), where Core would have registered it -- *tx-reconciliation* defaults to NIL (src/config.lisp:209), which is what keeps this narrow. Bounded overall because Core itself only ever writes 0 or 1, so this bites only another implementation's or a fuzzer's bytes; but it is a divergence in how we read the wire, and the generated :bool row spreads it to any future field. S3.
evidence: Container /Users/sen/common-lisp/bl-ga11v-misc-s3b, warm image, direct evals. (a) sendcmpct: parse-sendcmpct-payload on #(2 2 0 0 0 0 0 0 0) -> (NIL 2); on #(1 2 0 ...) -> (T 2); on #(0 2 0 ...) -> (NIL 2). So announce = 2 is read as 'do not announce'. (b) version: serialized make-version-message-bytes with :relay t (last byte 1), copied it and set the last byte to 2, read both back -- (:ORIG-LAST 1 :RELAY-WHEN-1 T :RELAY-WHEN-2 NIL). (c) consequence at the peer level: the same two payloads installed on an :outbound-full-relay peer give (:TX-RELAY-P-WHEN-1 T :TX-RELAY-P-WHEN-2 NIL), i.e. bl.net:peer-tx-relay-p says the fRelay=2 peer does not want transactions. Ours: src/serialization/message-macro.lisp:109; src/serialization/messages.lisp:206-210, :604-610; src/networking/peer.lisp:777-789, :880-887. Core: serialize.h:277; net_processing.cpp:3647, 3684-3705, 3907-3922.
fix_shape: Read a wire boolean the way Core does: not (zerop byte). Change the one generated row to `(/= (br-read-u8 br) 0)` (the writer already emits 1/0, which matches Core's `uint8_t f = a`), then delete the two hand-written repetitions of the same test by having them go through it -- the version message's relay :read form only needs the BIP37 absence default, so it becomes (if (> version 70001) (if (br-eof-p br) t (/= (br-read-u8 br) 0)) t), and parse-sendcmpct-payload becomes (values (/= announce 0) version). Nothing else changes: a nonzero-but-not-1 byte is not a protocol violation for Core, so it must not become one for us either. A serialization test should pin bytes 0, 1, 2 and 255 for both fields against Core's rule, and a peer-level test should assert peer-tx-relay-p is T for fRelay = 2, since the codec row alone would not have caught the two hand-written copies.
